title: Legal English onset-cluster table
spec_reference: Section 9 (Maximum Onset Principle against a fixed legal-onset table); Section 17 F5

reference.author: Kivisto-de Souza, Hanna
reference.title: Onset consonant clusters of General American English
reference.summarized_from_note: Table 1 states it is adapted/summarized from these three sources. Recorded verbatim as the provenance chain; Cruttenden describes SSBE but the table as published is General American, which the yod distribution confirms (no coronal+Y; SPY/SKY present, STY absent).

required_source_material: A named standard phonotactics reference giving the exhaustive inventory of legal English syllable-onset consonant clusters, mappable one-to-one onto the ARPAbet consonants in fixtures/lexicon/cmudict.symbols.

Candidates identified bibliographically: Roach, P., 'English Phonetics and Phonology: A Practical Course', 4th ed. (Cambridge University Press, 2009), ch. 8; Cruttenden, A., 'Gimson's Pronunciation of English' (Hodder), section 5.5. NEITHER was retrieved, so NEITHER has been used.

sourcing_findings.note: Established from bibliographic search only. No inventory was transcribed.
sourcing_findings.dialect_mismatch_warning: Roach and Cruttenden describe Standard Southern British English. The lexicon here is CMUdict, which is General American. The two differ in exactly the onsets this table governs: SSBE lists the three-consonant onsets /spj stj skj/ (as in 'stew' /stjuu/), which General American largely lacks through yod-dropping ('stew' = /stuu/). An SSBE inventory would admit onsets CMUdict never produces. Choose a General American description, or record the dialect deviation explicitly -- the onset inventory decides every syllable boundary the experiment produces.
rejected_substitutes: CMUdict word-initial frequency counts: a frequency-derived inventory is a different object from a phonotactic one -- it admits accidental gaps as illegal and rare loans as legal.
The PyPI 'syllabify' package (0.5.1): inspected, it syllabifies by sonority sequencing and carries no explicit legal-onset inventory. Not a phonotactics reference.

acceptance_requirements: Every entry is a sequence of ARPAbet CONSONANT symbols that may open a syllable.
Singleton onsets must be listed explicitly for every consonant that can begin a syllable -- the Maximum Onset Principle consults this table at every boundary, not only for clusters.
Two- and three-consonant clusters listed exhaustively for the chosen reference and dialect.
Every entry carries a non-empty 'source' and 'page_or_table'.
No cluster may be added to make a test pass. A cluster absent from this table is a hard error at syllabification.
how_to_populate: Fill fixtures/F5_onset_clusters/intake_f5.csv, then run: python3 tools/import_f5.py
